 JUDGMENT Wife, children and parents of Shivaramu D.M, filed petition under Section 166 of IMV Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.90,00,000/- from the SCCH-1 MVC No.1638/2023 respondents who are the owner and insurer of Car No.KA- 13-P-1736, alleging that on 13.03.2023 at about 9.45 p.m.,
when Shivaramu was standing on the side of Bellur cross road, in front of Green Park Dabha to cross the road, driver of a Car No.KA-13-P-1736 drove the same negligently, dashed the same to Shivaramu D.M thereby caused accident, caused grievous injuries to Shivaramu D.M., who succumbed to the injuries on the way to Adichunchanagiri Hospital, Bellur.
2. As on the date of the accident Shivaramu D.M being aged about 31 years use to earn Rs.30,000/-
per month by doing agriculture and vending milk.

3. Regarding the accident Bellur Police registered a case in Crime No.44/2023 against driver of car for the offence punishable under Sec.279, 304(A) IPC.
4.

In response to the notice, the respondent No.1 and 2 appeared through their respective Advocates filed separate written statements denying the allegations regarding the reason and mode of the accident, age, occupation and income of Shivaramu D.M. SCCH-1 MVC No.1638/2023 5.

sentences.text:
1 . Whether the petitioners prove that, on 13.03.2023 at about 9.45 p.m., in front of Green Park Dhaba, Bellur Cross, Namangala Taluk, Mandya, the death caused to one Shivaramu D.M., was due to actionable negligence act on the part of the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-P-1736 as alleged?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order?
6. On 12.1.2024, 26.3.2024, 04.7.2024, petitioner No.1 Ramya deposed as PW1 and produced 14 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.14.

On 31.7.2024, respondent No.1 deposed as RW.1 and produced 5 documents at Ex.R1 to R5.
7.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of petitioners and respondent No.1 and perused entire records.
On 7.12,.2024 respondent No.1 get filed notes of argument.

8. On the basis of the materials placed on record, my findings on the above issues are as under: -
Issue No.1 ...
In the Affirmative, Issue No.2...
Petitioners are entitle to receive Rs.37,09,000/- with current and future interest @ 6% p.a., as compensation, SCCH-1 MVC No.1638/2023 Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 9. Issue No.1:- In the evidence affidavit, PW1 Ramya W/o Shivaramu stated that on 13.03.2023 at about 9.45 p.m., when Shivaramu D.M was standing by the side of Bellur cross road in front of Green Park Dabha within the limits of Bellur Police station to cross the road, the driver of a Car No.KA-13-P-1736 drove the same negligently, dashed the same to Shivaramu D.M thereby caused accident, caused grievous injuries to Shivaramu D.M., who succumbed to the injuries on the way of Adichunchanagiri Hospital, Bellur.
10. In the written statements, respondent No.1 and 2 denied the allegation regarding the reason and mode of the accident.
11. In the cross-examination, PW1 stated that she never witnessed the accident.
Manjegowda who is the resident of neighbouring village filed the complaint.

PW.1 denied the suggestion that though the accident taken place SCCH-1 MVC No.1638/2023 due to the fault of her husband, in order to help them, Manjegowda has filed false complaint against the driver of the car.

12. In the evidence affidavit RW.1 the respondent No.1 stated that on 13.03.2023 when Sunil B.S.,
driving the car No. KA-13-P-1736 from Hassan towards Bengaluru at 9.30 PM at Bellur cross deceased suddenly crossed the main road (NH-75) without observing the vehicles running on the road in non-crossing area suffered accident, negligent crossing of the road was the reason for the Ramya D.G vs Narasimha Murthy N.S on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159614669/

sentences.text: In the cross-examination RW.1 stated that during accident he was sitting on the left seat of the car and the place of accident is Bengaluru-Hassan double way four lane NH-75.
RW.1 admitted that the place of accident is not a Zebra mark area or signal light area.
In this case, petitioners have not cross-examined RW.1.

14. Ex.P.1 is the copy of FIR and complaint pertaining to crime No.44/2023 registered by Bellur Police SCCH-1 MVC No.1638/2023 on 13.03.2023 at 23.50 hours against driver of Car No.KA- 13-P-1736 for having committed the offence punishable under Section 279, 304(A) of IPC.,
regarding the accident taken place on 13.03.2023 at 21.45 hours due to dashing of the car No.KA-13-P-1736 to Shivaramu resulting the death of Shivaramu on the basis of the complaint presented by Manjegowda S/o Venkataramu, resident of Bommanahalli, Bellur cross.
Ex.P.2 is the crime detail form.
Ex.P3 is the vehicle seizure mahazar dated 14.3.2023.
Ex.P4 is the copy of the sketch of the place of accident which shows that on the southern edge of East- West road accident taken place.
Ex.P5 is the Inquest mahazar.
Ex.P6 is the PM Report.
Ex.P7 is the Motor Vehicle Accident Report.

Ex.P8 is the copy of the chargesheet filed by Bellur police in Crime No.44/2023 against Sunil B.S. S/o Swamy, the driver of a Car No.KA- 13-P-1736 for having committed the offence punishable under Section 279, 304(A) of IPC., sec.187 of IMV Act.
In the police records name of Shivaramu D.M is noted as pedestrian and victim of the accident.
. In this case, there are no reasons to disbelieve the contents of the police records regarding the reason, mode and consequence of the accident.

Hence, I have concluded that on 13.03.2023 at 9.45 PM when Shivaramu was standing beside NH-75 at Bellur cross road in front of Green Park Dhabha in order to cross the road Sunil S/o Swamy negligently drove the car No.KA-13-P-1736 dashed the same to Shivaramu, thereby caused accident, caused grievous injuries to the Shivaramu, who succumbed to the injuries on the way to Adichunchanagiri Hospital, Bellur.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:

In the evidence PW.1 Ramya W/o Shivaramu stated that as on the date of accident,
her husband Shivaramu D.M being aged about 31 years, use to earn Rs.30,000/- by vending milk and by doing agriculture and use to contribute entire income to the family.

In the written statement,
respondents denied the allegation regarding age, occupation and income of the deceased.
In the cross-examination PW.1 denied the suggestion that as on the date of accident, her husband neither vending milk SCCH-1 MVC No.1638/2023 nor doing agriculture nor earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
PW.1 admitted non-availability of documents regarding the income of her husband.
In the evidence RW.1 the respondent No.1 owner of the car stated nothing regarding the occupation and income of the deceased.
17. In the police records, age of the deceased is noted as 32 years.
In the copy of the Adhar card marked at Ex.P14 date of birth of Shivaramu is noted as 06.06.1991.
The Adhar card shows that petitioners are the wife, children and parents of Shivaramu.

Hence, I have calculated the loss of Ramya D.G vs Narasimha Murthy N.S on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159614669/

Hence, I award Rs.34,56,000/- towards loss of dependency, Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate,
Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.2,20,000 (Rs.44,000/- x 5) towards loss of consortium.
Hence, I award Rs.37,09,000/- with current and future interest @ 6% p.a., to the petitioners as compensation.
18. Evidence of the RW.1 respondent No.1, copy of the policy marked at Ex.R2 shows that as on the date of accident car No. KA-13-P-1736 had insurance coverage with respondent No.2.
Copy of the Driving Licence marked at Ex.R4 shows that as on the date of accident Sunil B.S. S/o Swamy had licence to drive the Light Motor Vehicles (Car).

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being owner and insurer of the car No. KA-13-P-1736 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioners.

sentences.text: The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.

The respondents No.1 and 2 shall either jointly or severally liable to pay Rs.37,09,000/- (Rupees thirty seven lakhs nine thousand only) with current and future interest @ 6% p.a., to the petitioners towards compensation.
The respondent No.2 insurer of the car No. KA-13-P- 1736 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within three months from today.
Compensation and interest are distributed among the petitioners equally.

After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest allotted in favour of the petitioner No.1 and 4, the wife and father of deceased may be released by crediting the same to their bank account directly.

After deposit of the compensation amount, 50% compensation allotted in favour of Puttananjamma mother SCCH-1 MVC No.1638/2023 of the deceased may be released by crediting the same to her bank account directly.
Surplus compensation and interest allotted in favour of Puttananjamma shall be deposited in any bank for a period of two years without permitting to create any encumbrance.

The entire compensation and interest allotted in favour of petitioner No.2 Sahana D.S., petitioner No.3 Dimpana D.S., minor children of the petitioner No.1 and deceased shall be deposited in any bank till they are attaining the age of 19 years without permitting to create any encumbrance however reserving liberty to petitioner No.1 Ramya, the mother to withdraw periodical interest once in three months in accordance with law.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an Award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer Gr.I, transcribed by him, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 10th day of December, 2024)

(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge,
Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T. Bangalore.
